record.title: Aikido reports a 328 GB pruned GLM-5.3 security model with near-parent CVE recall
record.summary: Aikido released Altar-1, a 328 GB W4A16/REAP-pruned derivative of GLM-5.3 intended for local defensive-security workloads. Aikido reports that pruning reduces its already-quantized parent from 488.2 GB to 328.0 GB while retaining 60.4% average recall per run, versus 61.5% for the parent, on an internal benchmark of 32 known vulnerabilities across 30 repositories with three runs per case. Both versions rediscovered the same 23 vulnerabilities at least once. The vendor says the model is configured for vLLM on four H200 GPUs. These are company-reported results from targeted known-CVE rediscovery inside a larger pipeline; they do not demonstrate blind vulnerability discovery, exploit validation, patch quality or independent performance.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Aikido reports that Altar-1 starts from GLM-5.3 AWQ INT4 and uses REAP expert pruning to reduce stored weights from 488.2 GB to 328.0 GB, retaining 168 of 256 routed experts per layer. Relative to the unpruned 1,506.7 GB BF16 parent, the reported storage reduction is 78.2%.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On Aikido’s internal benchmark of 32 known vulnerabilities across 30 repositories, with three runs per case, Altar-1 averaged 60.4% recall per run and rediscovered 23/32 vulnerabilities at least once across three runs. The GLM-5.3 AWQ INT4 parent averaged 61.5% recall and covered the same 23/32; the full-precision parent averaged 65.6% and covered 25/32.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: Aikido defines this as targeted CVE rediscovery within a pipeline that uses other models for surrounding stages. It does not measure blind discovery across a codebase, exploit validation, or fix proposals. The published evaluation is an internal vendor benchmark and has not been independently reproduced in this review.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Aikido publishes Altar-1 model weights and documents a vLLM serving configuration targeting four NVIDIA H200 GPUs; its model card identifies the model as a 504B-parameter, W4A16 pruned GLM-5.3 derivative.

evidence_gaps.description: The recall and coverage comparison comes from Aikido’s internal 32-CVE benchmark and has not been independently reproduced or adjudicated.
The release does not report false-positive rates, serving latency/throughput, resource cost, or quality on unknown-vulnerability discovery and remediation tasks.

brief.importance_rationale: If Aikido’s task-specific evaluation generalizes, pruning can make a large open-weight security model fit a four-H200 node with little reported recall loss against its quantized parent, a useful serving and privacy option for some defensive workflows. The impact is meaningful but narrow: the benchmark is small, internal, and measures known-vulnerability rediscovery rather than broad pentesting.
limitations: All model-performance figures in the release are Aikido-reported; no independent replication was located or performed.
The evaluation covers 32 known vulnerabilities in 30 repositories with three runs per case and is not a blind discovery test.
The benchmark runs within Aikido’s larger pipeline, which uses other models for surrounding stages; it isolates neither the security model’s complete product contribution nor human review effects.
The report gives recall and coverage but no precision, false-positive rates, exploit-validation outcomes, patch quality, runtime, throughput or serving cost.
A four-H200 serving target documents a feasible configuration claimed by the model provider; it is not a measured minimum hardware requirement or independently verified production profile.
brief.summary: Aikido released Altar-1, a 328 GB W4A16/REAP-pruned derivative of GLM-5.3 intended for local defensive-security workloads. Aikido reports that pruning reduces its already-quantized parent from 488.2 GB to 328.0 GB while retaining 60.4% average recall per run, versus 61.5% for the parent, on an internal benchmark of 32 known vulnerabilities across 30 repositories with three runs per case. Both versions rediscovered the same 23 vulnerabilities at least once. The vendor says the model is configured for vLLM on four H200 GPUs. These are company-reported results from targeted known-CVE rediscovery inside a larger pipeline; they do not demonstrate blind vulnerability discovery, exploit validation, patch quality or independent performance.

technical.claimed_result: Aikido reports stored weights of 1,506.7 GB for full-precision GLM-5.3, 488.2 GB for the AWQ INT4 parent, and 328.0 GB for Altar-1. It reports average per-run recall of 65.6%, 61.5%, and 60.4%, respectively, on its internal known-CVE benchmark. Altar and the AWQ parent each covered 23 of 32 vulnerabilities at least once over three runs; full-precision GLM-5.3 covered 25.
technical.compute_or_cost: The sources report stored weight sizes and a four-H200 serving target, but do not provide measured latency, throughput, energy use, serving cost, memory headroom under a specified production workload, or comparison of total hardware cost.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public model card and weights document the released Altar-1 artifact, its W4A16/REAP configuration and a four-H200 vLLM serving target. This verifies model availability and declared configuration, not the vendor’s performance claims.
technical.implementation_status: Aikido publishes Altar-1 weights on Hugging Face and documents use in vLLM on four NVIDIA H200 GPUs. The company says it deployed the model in its Aikido Machine fleet; this is a company report, not an independently inspected deployment.
technical.mechanism: Aikido applies AWQ INT4 quantization to routed experts in GLM-5.3, then uses REAP contribution scores and a domain-preserving selection strategy to remove 88 of 256 routed experts per layer without retraining. The remaining model keeps eight routed experts active per token.
technical.regime: Aikido’s internal benchmark covers 32 known vulnerabilities across 30 repositories and three runs per case. The company describes it as targeted rediscovery inside a larger AI Code Analysis pipeline that uses other models for surrounding stages. The model card documents a vLLM configuration for four H200 GPUs.
technical.reproducibility: Aikido links a public fidelity study and pruning toolkit, and the model card exposes weights and serving instructions. This review did not execute the model, inspect raw run outputs, or independently reproduce the CVE benchmark. The benchmark’s known-cases and internal pipeline limit external validation.
technical.strongest_baseline: The closest compression baseline is the same GLM-5.3 checkpoint quantized with AWQ INT4 before REAP pruning: Aikido reports 488.2 GB, 61.5% mean recall per run and 23/32 vulnerabilities covered at least once, compared with Altar-1 at 328.0 GB, 60.4% and 23/32. The benchmark is internal and the evaluation has not been independently replicated.

brief.title: Aikido reports a 328 GB pruned GLM-5.3 security model with near-parent CVE recall
brief.why_it_matters: The result gives a concrete example of trading model weight storage against task-specific security recall: Aikido reports another 32.8% reduction against an already-quantized parent with about a 1.1 percentage-point lower mean recall on its internal benchmark. If independently confirmed, this could lower the hardware threshold for local defensive-security inference. The test does not establish that the model finds unknown vulnerabilities or performs a complete penetration test.
